tasks.title: MAC of a tapered wing
tasks.statement: Wing panel: root chord **{cr} mm**, taper ratio λ = c_t/c_r = **{lam}**. Find the mean aerodynamic chord (mm).
tasks.solution: MAC = ⅔·c_r·(1 + λ + λ²)/(1 + λ). At λ = 1 (a rectangle) the MAC equals the chord; with taper it lies between the root and tip chords, closer to the root.

tasks.title: Flying wing CG
tasks.statement: A flying wing: root chord **{cr} mm**, tip chord **{ct} mm**, semispan **{bh} mm**, leading-edge sweep **{sw}°**. Find the CG position from the leading edge of the root chord (mm) for a static margin of **{sm}** MAC (the NP is at 25 % MAC).
tasks.solution: λ = c_t/c_r; MAC = ⅔·c_r·(1+λ+λ²)/(1+λ); y_MAC = (b/2)/3·(1+2λ)/(1+λ); x_LE = y_MAC·tan Λ. CG = x_LE + (0.25 − SM)·MAC. A quarter of the root chord does not work here: it ignores the aft shift of the MAC due to sweep.

tasks.title: Battery shift to move the CG
tasks.statement: The CG of an airplane of **{m} kg** must move forward by **{d} mm**. A battery of **{mb} kg** is the only movable mass. How many millimeters must the battery move?
tasks.solution: The moment M·Δx_CG = m_batt·Δx_batt, hence Δx_batt = d·M/m_batt. A light battery in a heavy airplane has to travel far: if there is not enough travel, move other components.

tasks.title: C_D0 from a glide test
tasks.statement: An airplane of **{m} kg**, wing area 0.41 m², span 1.83 m, Oswald factor 0.8. A glide with the motor off at **{v} m/s** gave L/D = **{ld}**. Find C_D0 (ρ = 1.225 kg/m³, g = 9.81).
tasks.solution: C_L = 2mg/(ρV²S); C_D = C_L/(L/D); k = 1/(π·e·AR), AR = b²/S; C_D0 = C_D − k·C_L². For a foam FPV airplane with a camera, 0.02–0.06 is reasonable.
